changes_made.explanation: Normalized CNN/DM to CNN/DailyMail and simplified output descriptions. Removed duplicate output descriptions.
Normalized metric names to standard forms and removed redundant/alternative names. All metrics mentioned are used for evaluating faithfulness of generated summaries.
Paper does not use LLMs as judges for evaluation. LLMs were not used in this capacity in 2020 when this paper was published.

guideline: Hierarchical annotation process: First evaluate grammaticality (meaningful vs nonsensical), then for meaningful sentences evaluate grammatical correctness, then for grammatical sentences evaluate faithfulness, with follow-up categorization of unfaithfulness type (hallucination vs contradiction)

changes_made.explanation: Kept existing guideline and criteria as they accurately reflect the human evaluation methodology described in the paper.

overall_notes: The extraction was generally accurate. The paper focuses on faithfulness evaluation for abstractive summarization, comparing various automatic metrics against human judgments. Key contributions include the FEQA metric and analysis of the abstractiveness-faithfulness trade-off. Metadata needed minor normalization and deduplication but was fundamentally correct.
